page: Vultr vcg-l40s-32c-375g-96vram is a dedicated GPU-accelerated cloud server instance configured for compute-intensive and machine learning workloads. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6448H processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, built on the x86_64 architecture. The host provides 375.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 11.72 GB per core, along with 2200 GB of NVMe SSD local storage and 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. Its primary acceleration is driven by two NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPUs delivering a combined 96 GB of GDDR6 VRAM.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong multi-threaded and GPU-accelerated performance across the board. The server achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,668.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 64,768.69, bolstered by hardware vector instruction sets including AVX-512 VNNI and BF16. In LLM inference benchmarks, the dual-L40S setup achieves top-tier results (top 10%), processing 13,643.47 tokens per second for prompt ingestion on a 135M parameter model and 6,275.36 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model. Memory subsystem measurements confirm high throughput, reaching 211.9 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth, while Redis operations attained 70.17 million SET operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server concentrates substantial GPU memory (96 GB) and high host RAM (375 GB) into a single dual-socket GPU footprint, making it an efficient platform for mid-sized LLM inference and graphics workloads compared to deploying multiple smaller instances. A notable operational tradeoff is the Intel Xeon 6448H base clock rate of 2.0 GHz without Hyper-Threading enabled (1 thread per core), which yields average single-core CPU throughput on stress-ng tests while excelling in aggregate parallel execution.

This hardware profile is well-suited for high-throughput LLM inference, AI model fine-tuning, ray tracing, 3D image processing pipelines, and in-memory database services requiring substantial local NVMe storage and high GPU memory density.
